settings.protocol_note: REDUCED PROTOCOL: enrich_exhaustiveness 8 instead of 32, enrich_n_seeds 1 instead of 3. These numbers are not the protocol's own and should be regenerated before publication: unset DOCK_ENRICH_EXHAUSTIVENESS DOCK_ENRICH_N_SEEDS and re-run step 06 on hardware with more cores. Scores are insensitive to exhaustiveness in this pocket set (8, 16 and 32 agree to 0.01 kcal/mol on a test ligand), and the enrichment control's uncertainty is the bootstrap CI over compounds rather than the per-ligand search spread, so a reduced enrichment budget costs the replicate error bars and not the ranking itself.

EGFR.rmsd_method: RDKit CalcRMS, symmetry-corrected heavy atoms, in place (no superposition); the molecules are matched on the heavy-atom graph because the crystal reference and the Open Babel pose perceive bond orders differently

FGFR4.sampling: random within class, MW-matched; NOT potency extremes
FGFR4.inactive_class: measured weak binders; no censored '>' records in the committed data, so re-run step 01 with network access to populate a true inactive class
FGFR4.metric_caveat: Top 1% of 99 compounds is 1 compound, and the active fraction is 0.51, not the ~1% that EF and BEDROC were designed for. Read each metric against its null_baselines entry: exceeds_null is whether the value falls outside the middle 90% of what a random ranking gives on this same design.

score_comparability_note: AutoDock Vina scores are empirical and receptor-specific. They are not transferable binding free energies, so a weaker score in one pocket than another is not evidence of selectivity. Compare within a target (see the <T>_vina_z columns), and treat any score weaker than -4.0 kcal/mol as a placement failure to investigate, not as a measured steric clash.
